question: 人生该规划，还是走着瞧？
question_en: Should you plan your life, or find out as you go?
sub: 点只能回头连，可回头连上的，会不会只是事后挑出来的那几个点？
sub_en: The dots only connect looking back, but are the ones we connect just the few we picked out afterwards?

casting.reason: 『点只能回头连』这句话就是他说的。他对产品偏执到每颗螺丝，对人生却主张别画路线，只信直觉、跟着热爱走，相信那些点将来自会连上。
casting.reason_en: 'You can only connect the dots looking backwards' is his line. Obsessive about every screw in a product, he argues that a life shouldn't be mapped: trust your gut, follow what you love, and believe the dots will connect later.

casting.reason: 他是『以终为始』的人：凡事先在心里造一遍，再在现实里造一遍。他要的不是十年日程表，而是一枚能在岔路口指方向的指南针。
casting.reason_en: He is the 'begin with the end in mind' man: everything is created twice, first in the mind and then in the world. What he wants is not a ten-year schedule but a compass that points the way at every fork.

casting.reason: 他把规划看成庙算：先算清己方能做什么、不能做什么，立于不败之地，再因势而变。在他这里，计划与随机应变本来就是一回事。
casting.reason_en: He treats planning as the war-council reckoning: first work out what you can and cannot do, make yourself impossible to defeat, then shift with circumstances. For him, plan and improvisation were never opposites.

casting.reason: 他最不信长期预测，嘲笑事后连线是叙事谬误加幸存者偏差。他的方案是杠铃：大头求稳、绝不爆仓，小头撒大量下行有限、上行无限的小赌注。
casting.reason_en: He trusts no long-range forecast and mocks after-the-fact dot-connecting as narrative fallacy plus survivorship bias. His answer is the barbell: keep the bulk safe and never risk ruin, and scatter many small bets with capped downside and open upside.

casting.reason: 他用裂脑实验里的『解释器』拆穿两边：回头连线是左脑事后编故事，向前规划用的也是同一个讲故事的器官。他还带来一条反直觉的数据：退路留得越多，人越难爱上已选的那条路。
casting.reason_en: He uses the 'interpreter' from his split-brain work to unmask both sides: connecting the dots is the left brain telling a story after the fact, and planning ahead runs on the same storytelling organ. He also brings a counterintuitive finding: the more exits you keep open, the harder it is to love the road you chose.

casting.reason: 『人生只能向后理解，却必须向前活。』他认为真正的危险不是计划不周，而是永远不选、把所有可能都留着的审美式人生——不选择，本身就是选择。
casting.reason_en: 'Life can only be understood backwards, but it must be lived forwards.' For him the real danger is not a poor plan but the aesthetic life that never chooses and keeps every possibility open; not choosing is itself a choice.

casting.reason: 他从『初心』出发，把问题轻轻转了个方向：计划可以有，麻烦在于『得到什么』的念头，把此刻活成了通往别处的过道。
casting.reason_en: Starting from 'beginner's mind', he turns the question gently aside: plans are fine; the trouble is the gaining idea, which turns the present moment into a corridor to somewhere else.

posts.text: 我退学后蹭了一门书法课，纯粹因为它美。十年后设计第一台Mac，那些字体全回来了。当年要是有人问我学这个有什么用，我答不上来。所以我说，**点只能回头连，你只能相信它们将来会连上**——信你的直觉、命运、业力，随便叫什么。别误会，做产品我计划到每颗螺丝；可人生不是产品，没有需求文档。
posts.text_en: After I dropped out I sat in on a calligraphy class, purely because it was beautiful. Ten years later, designing the first Mac, all those typefaces came back. If anyone had asked me back then what it was for, I'd have had no answer. That's why I say **you can only connect the dots looking backwards; you have to trust that they'll connect later**: your gut, destiny, karma, call it what you like. Don't get me wrong, with a product I plan down to the last screw. But a life isn't a product. It doesn't come with a requirements doc.

glossary.业力: karma（业力）：佛教说法，指人的所作所为会留下后果、牵动日后的境遇。

glossary_en.karma: In Buddhist and Hindu thought, the idea that what you do leaves consequences that shape what later happens to you.

posts.text: 凡事都创造两次：先在心里，再在现实里。你不先在心里造，别人就替你造——老板、父母、广告，照他们的剧本活。**我说的以终为始，要的是指南针，不是地图。**地图会过时，路会改道；可你想成为怎样的父亲、朋友、同事，二十年都不该变。不知道终点，至少知道方向，岔路口才不会只挑最省力的那条。
posts.text_en: Everything is created twice: first in the mind, then in the world. If you don't do the first creation yourself, someone else will do it for you, your boss, your parents, the ads, and you'll live by their script. **Begin with the end in mind means a compass, not a map.** Maps go out of date and roads get rerouted, but the kind of father, friend or colleague you want to be shouldn't change in twenty years. You may not know the destination, but if you know the direction, you won't just take the easiest path at every fork.

glossary.以终为始: begin with the end in mind（以终为始）：柯维七个习惯之二，先想清自己最终想成为什么样的人，再据此安排眼前。

glossary_en.Begin with the end in mind: The second of Covey's seven habits: get clear on who you ultimately want to be, then arrange the present around it.

posts.text: 夫未战而庙算胜者，得算多也；多算胜，少算不胜，而况于无算乎！然兵无常势，水无常形。所算者，非敌之必至，乃己之所能与所不能也。**先为不可胜，以待敌之可胜。**人之一生亦然：立于不败之地，而后因势取之。无算而往，谓之赌；算而不变，谓之愚。
posts.text_en: The side that wins the reckoning in the temple before battle has made more calculations; more calculation wins, less loses, and none at all, how much worse! Yet war has no fixed shape, as water has no fixed form. What you calculate is not where the enemy must come, but what you yourself can and cannot do. **First make yourself impossible to defeat, then wait for the enemy to become defeatable.** A life is the same: stand where you cannot lose, then take what the situation offers. To go without calculating is gambling; to calculate and never change is folly.
posts.vernacular: 仗还没打，在庙堂上推演就先赢了的，是因为算得周全；算得多的赢，算得少的输，何况根本不算！可是用兵没有固定的态势，就像水没有固定的形状。要算的不是敌人一定会从哪儿来，而是自己能做什么、做不到什么。**先让自己立于不败，再等对方露出可胜之机。**人这一辈子也一样：先站稳不会垮的位置，再顺着形势去拿。不算就上，那是赌博；算了却死守不变，那是愚蠢。

glossary.庙算: temple reckoning（庙算）：古代出兵前在宗庙里比较敌我形势、估算胜负，即战前的全局谋划。
glossary.不可胜: invincibility（不可胜）：先让自己没有可被击败的破绽；能不能胜在敌，能不能不败在己。

glossary_en.reckoning in the temple: In ancient China, before a campaign, the rulers compared their strength with the enemy's in the ancestral temple and estimated the odds: strategic planning before battle.
glossary_en.impossible to defeat: Sunzi's idea that you first remove every weakness the enemy could exploit; victory depends on the enemy, but not losing depends on you.

posts.text: 那段书法课的故事，是叙事谬误加幸存者偏差。一千个退学蹭课的人，九百九十九个没做出Mac，他们没被请去斯坦福演讲。可五年规划更糟：它假装你能预测，而改变人生的往往是黑天鹅。**别预测，去布局可选权。**杠铃：九成放在绝不爆仓的稳妥处，一成撒小赌注——下行有限、上行无限。剩下唯一要规划的，是别破产。
posts.text_en: That calligraphy story is the narrative fallacy plus survivorship bias. Of a thousand dropouts sitting in on classes, nine hundred and ninety-nine never built a Mac, and nobody invited them to give a Stanford commencement speech. But the five-year plan is worse: it pretends you can predict, when what changes a life is usually a Black Swan. **Don't predict; build optionality.** The barbell: ninety percent somewhere that can never blow up, ten percent scattered across small bets with limited downside and unlimited upside. The only thing left to plan is not going bust.

glossary.叙事谬误: narrative fallacy（叙事谬误）：人忍不住给一串事件编出因果故事，让偶然看起来像必然。
glossary.幸存者偏差: survivorship bias（幸存者偏差）：只看见成功留下来的样本，把失败而沉默的大多数漏掉。
glossary.黑天鹅: Black Swan（黑天鹅）：罕见、事前难以预料、影响巨大，事后却被人说成早该想到的事件。
glossary.可选权: optionality（可选权）：保留『有权而无义务』的机会，好事来了可以接，坏事来了损失有限。
glossary.杠铃: barbell strategy（杠铃策略）：两头极端、避开中间——一头极保守，一头小额高风险。

glossary_en.narrative fallacy: Our urge to weave a causal story around a string of events, so that chance looks like destiny.
glossary_en.survivorship bias: Looking only at the successes that survived and missing the silent majority who failed.
glossary_en.Black Swan: A rare, unforeseeable event with enormous impact that people later claim they should have seen coming.
glossary_en.optionality: Holding the right but not the obligation to act, so you can take the upside while the downside stays limited.
glossary_en.barbell: Taleb's strategy of combining two extremes and avoiding the middle: one side very safe, the other small and high-risk.

posts.text: 我们给裂脑病人的右脑看雪景，左脑看鸡爪，他左手挑了铲子。问他为什么，掌管语言的左脑根本没见过雪，却立刻答：铲子用来清鸡棚。**回头连上的线，多半是左脑解释器事后编的。**它不撒谎，它真心相信。麻烦在于，向前规划用的也是同一个讲故事的器官。两边都在讲故事，区别只在于你知不知道那是故事。
posts.text_en: We showed a split-brain patient's right hemisphere a snow scene and his left hemisphere a chicken claw, and his left hand picked a shovel. Asked why, his left hemisphere, which handles language and had never seen the snow, answered at once: you need a shovel to clean out the chicken shed. **The line you draw back through the dots is mostly written after the fact by the left brain's interpreter.** It isn't lying; it sincerely believes it. The catch is that planning ahead runs on the same storytelling organ. Both sides are telling stories. The only difference is whether you know it's a story.

glossary.裂脑: split brain（裂脑）：为治癫痫切断连接左右大脑半球的胼胝体，两边各自接收信息、互不相通。
glossary.解释器: interpreter（解释器）：加扎尼加对左脑一种功能的命名，它会为自己并不知情的行为当场编出合理解释。

glossary_en.split-brain: A patient whose corpus callosum, the bridge between the brain's hemispheres, has been cut to treat epilepsy, so each side takes in information the other cannot see.
glossary_en.interpreter: Gazzaniga's name for a left-hemisphere function that instantly invents a plausible explanation for behaviour it knows nothing about.

posts.text: 我在日记里写过：人生只能向后理解，却必须向前活。所以计划与走着瞧之争，都没碰到要害。真正的危险是第三种人：他把所有门都开着，今天想这，明天想那，**永远在可能性里徘徊，于是谁也没成为。**这就是审美的人生。要么这样，要么那样——你必须选，选择本身才造出一个自我。不选，也是一种选择，而且是最糟的那种。
posts.text_en: I wrote in my journal that life can only be understood backwards, but it must be lived forwards. So the fight between planning and drifting misses the point. The real danger is a third kind of person, who keeps every door open, wants this today and that tomorrow, and **hovers forever among possibilities, and so never becomes anyone.** That is the aesthetic life. Either/or: you must choose, and only the choosing makes a self. Not choosing is also a choice, and the worst one.

glossary.审美的人生: aesthetic life（审美的人生）：克尔凯郭尔人生三阶段之一，追逐新鲜与可能、逃避承诺，以免被任何一种生活定型。
glossary.要么这样，要么那样: Either/Or（非此即彼）：克尔凯郭尔的书名，主张人必须在根本的生活方式之间作出抉择。

glossary_en.aesthetic life: The first of Kierkegaard's three stages of life: chasing novelty and possibility and dodging commitment so as never to be pinned down.
glossary_en.Either/or: The title of Kierkegaard's book, arguing that a person must make a decisive choice between ways of life.

posts.text: 初学者的心里有许多可能，专家的心里只剩很少。计划没有错，就像知道去禅堂的路。可是走路的时候，就只是走路。麻烦不在计划，而在『得到什么』的念头：为了十年后的样子，把今天当成过道匆匆穿过。**规划可以有，只是别把此刻当成通往别处的路。**到了那里，你也会把那里当过道。
posts.text_en: In the beginner's mind there are many possibilities; in the expert's mind there are few. There's nothing wrong with a plan, any more than with knowing the way to the zendo. But when you walk, just walk. The trouble isn't the plan; it's the gaining idea, hurrying through today like a corridor for the sake of who you'll be in ten years. **Make plans if you like, just don't treat this moment as a road to somewhere else.** When you get there, you'll treat that place as a corridor too.

glossary.初学者的心: beginner's mind（初心）：铃木俊隆最核心的教导，像初学者那样不预设、不自满，对一切保持开放。
glossary.『得到什么』的念头: gaining idea（求得之心）：铃木俊隆的说法，做事时总惦记着能换来什么结果，于是错过了事情本身。

glossary_en.beginner's mind: Suzuki's central teaching: meeting everything as a beginner does, without assumptions or self-satisfaction, open to whatever comes.
glossary_en.gaining idea: Suzuki's term for doing something with your mind fixed on what it will get you, and so missing the thing itself.

posts.text: @加扎尼加 就算那条线是事后编的，又怎样？要紧的不是线准不准，是你当时敢不敢。我退学那年吓坏了，学费花的是养父母一辈子的积蓄；撑住我的，正是『它总会有用』这个故事。**故事不必是真的，它只要让你敢全情投入。**全情投入的人，才会攒下值得连的点。你们分析得都对，可分析从来没让谁退过学。
posts.text_en: @Gazzaniga So what if the line is written afterwards? What matters isn't whether it's accurate but whether you dared at the time. The year I dropped out I was terrified; my adoptive parents' whole savings were going on my tuition. What held me up was exactly that story: it'll turn out useful somehow. **The story doesn't have to be true; it only has to let you go all in.** Only people who go all in collect dots worth connecting. Your analyses are all correct, but analysis never got anyone to drop out.

posts.text: @塔勒布 九成稳妥、一成小赌，这本身就是一份计划，而且是很好的计划。可你只管下注，不管为什么下注。没有价值排序的可选权，结果就是什么都答应：每个饭局都去，每个副业都试，**最后挤掉的，是孩子的晚饭和你自己的睡眠。**要事第一，就是先把大石头放进罐子，再撒你的小石子。
posts.text_en: @Taleb Ninety percent safe, ten percent small bets: that is itself a plan, and a very good one. But you only care about placing bets, not about why. Optionality without a ranking of values ends in saying yes to everything: every dinner, every side hustle, **and what gets squeezed out in the end is your kids' dinner and your own sleep.** Put first things first: get the big rocks into the jar, then scatter your pebbles.

glossary.要事第一: put first things first（要事第一）：柯维七个习惯之三，先安排重要而不紧急的事，再处理其余。

glossary_en.Put first things first: The third of Covey's seven habits: schedule what is important but not urgent before everything else.

posts.text: 子言必择，善。然择于未知，是以卒试将也。兵法曰：**知可以战与不可以战者胜。**合于利而动，不合于利而止。吾亦言『投之亡地然后存』，然此乃迫于九地之势，非常法也。先察地形，量己粮秣，而后跃之。跃而无退路者，或成或亡；智者不以一跃赌全军。
posts.text_en: You say one must choose. Good. But to choose blind is to test a general by throwing him into battle. The Art of War says: **he wins who knows when he can fight and when he cannot.** Move when it serves you; stop when it does not. I too said 'throw them into a place with no way out and they will survive', but that is forced by the terrain, not the rule. Survey the ground, count your provisions, then leap. A leap with no retreat ends in triumph or in ruin; the wise do not stake the whole army on one jump.
posts.vernacular: 你说人必须选择，说得好。可是在什么都不清楚的时候选，就像把还没练过的兵直接推上战场来考将领。兵法说：**知道什么时候能打、什么时候不能打的，才会赢。**有利就动，不利就停。我也说过『把军队投到无路可退的绝境，反而能活』，但那是被地形逼出来的，不是常规打法。先看清地形，掂量自己的粮草，再纵身一跃。没有退路的一跃，要么成要么灭；聪明人不会拿一跳去押上整支军队。

glossary.九地: nine terrains（九地）：《孙子兵法》按处境把战地分为九类，『死地』是其中背水而战、不战即亡之地。

glossary_en.terrain: The Art of War sorts battlegrounds into nine situations; 'death ground' is where you have your back to the wall and must fight or perish.

posts.text: @乔布斯 『故事让你敢』——问题是，同一个故事也让九百九十九个人敢了，他们敢完就没了。**你的建议是幸存者给的，失败者没有毕业典礼。**我不反对冒险，我反对拿房子和健康冒险。你退学，好歹还蹭着课、睡朋友地板，下行有底；今天有人借网贷去追梦，那不叫勇气，叫爆仓。
posts.text_en: @Jobs 'The story lets you dare'. The problem is that the same story let nine hundred and ninety-nine others dare too, and after daring they were gone. **Your advice comes from a survivor; the failures don't get commencement speeches.** I'm not against risk. I'm against risking your house and your health. When you dropped out you still audited classes and slept on friends' floors, so your downside had a floor. Someone today taking out an online loan to chase a dream isn't brave. That's a blow-up.

posts.text: @塔勒布 有个实验值得你看。吉尔伯特让学生冲印照片挑一张带走，一组可以几天内换，一组当场定死。可以换的那组，**后来对自己那张照片更不满意。**退路是有心理成本的：留着别的门，大脑就一直在比较，没法安顿下来爱上已选的那条路。事业上多留选项也许划算，可婚姻、友谊、手艺，未必。
posts.text_en: @Taleb There's an experiment you should look at. Daniel Gilbert had students print photos and keep one; one group could swap within days, the other's choice was final on the spot. The group that could swap **ended up liking their photo less.** Exits have a psychological cost: with other doors open, the brain keeps comparing and never settles into loving the road it took. Keeping options may pay in a career, but in a marriage, a friendship or a craft, perhaps not.

posts.text: @铃木 你说走路时就只是走路，我很喜欢。但当心，审美者也最爱『此刻』：今天这个此刻美，明天那个此刻也美，他一个个享用，从不为任何一个负责。我说的瞬间，**是永恒碰到时间、人必须决断的那一刻。**扫地时只是扫地，很好；可总有一天，你得决定这一生扫哪座寺。
posts.text_en: @Suzuki 'When you walk, just walk'. I like that very much. But be careful: the aesthete loves 'the present moment' most of all. This moment is lovely today, that one tomorrow; he savours them one by one and answers for none. The instant I mean **is where eternity touches time and a person must decide.** Sweeping while you sweep is fine; but one day you have to decide which temple you'll sweep for life.

glossary.瞬间: the instant（瞬间，丹麦语 Øieblikket）：克尔凯郭尔的概念，永恒与时间相交、人作出决断的那一点。

glossary_en.instant: Kierkegaard's Øieblikket: the point where eternity intersects time and a person makes a decisive choice.

posts.text: @乔布斯 你常说『求知若饥』。饥饿很有力量，可饥饿的心总在找下一顿，吃完这顿就惦记那顿。初心不是饿，**初心是一只空碗：不急着装满，所以什么都能接住。**你说那堂书法课纯粹因为它美——那一刻你没在求什么，那就是初心。后来那些点连上，是因为你当时没在连。
posts.text_en: @Jobs You like to say 'stay hungry'. Hunger is powerful, but a hungry mind is always looking for the next meal; as soon as it finishes one it's thinking of another. Beginner's mind isn't hunger. **Beginner's mind is an empty bowl: it isn't in a hurry to be filled, so it can receive anything.** You said you took that calligraphy class purely because it was beautiful. In that moment you weren't seeking anything; that was beginner's mind. The dots connected later because back then you weren't trying to connect them.

posts.text: 我收回一半：塔勒布说得对，我当年下行有底，这一点该先讲。所以顺序是：先把开销压低，低到你付得起好奇。然后，**每年至少做一件纯粹因为着迷、不问用处的事**——一门课、一个手艺、一次长途。最后，每天早上照镜子问：如果今天是最后一天，我还愿意做今天要做的事吗？连着太多天说不，就该换点什么了。点会不会连上，交给以后；你现在只管让每个点都是真心选的。
posts.text_en: I'll take back half of it. Taleb is right: my downside had a floor back then, and I should have said that first. So the order is: first get your costs down, low enough that you can afford curiosity. Then **every year, do at least one thing purely because it fascinates you, without asking what it's for**: a class, a craft, a long trip. And every morning look in the mirror and ask: if today were my last day, would I want to do what I'm about to do today? If the answer is no for too many days in a row, change something. Whether the dots connect is for later. Your job now is just to make sure each dot is one you truly chose.

posts.text: 我接受塔勒布的杠铃、加扎尼加的照片：方向要定，路线要松，该定死的就定死。具体做三件事。第一，写一页纸：想象八十岁生日，家人、朋友、同事各会怎么说你，这就是你的指南针。第二，别做十年规划，**做周计划：每周日按角色挑出两三块大石头，先排进日程。**第三，每季度对一次指南针，路线随便改，方向别轻易改。
posts.text_en: I'll take Taleb's barbell and Gazzaniga's photos: fix the direction, keep the route loose, and lock in what deserves locking in. Three concrete things. First, write one page: imagine your eightieth birthday and what your family, friends and colleagues would say about you. That's your compass. Second, skip the ten-year plan and **plan by the week: every Sunday, pick two or three big rocks for each of your roles and put them in the calendar first.** Third, check the compass once a quarter. Change the route as often as you like; change the direction rarely.

posts.text: 合众论而言之：计者，非绘必由之途，乃立不败之地也。其一，**先为不可胜：储半岁之粮，不以宅与身为注。**其二，岁一庙算：己之长短、势之所趋、可以战与不可以战者，书之于册。其三，以正合，以奇胜：正者，饭碗也；奇者，小试也，败亦无伤。至于连点成线，胜后之言耳，不足为法。
posts.text_en: To sum up all that has been said: a plan is not a drawing of the road you must take; it is the ground on which you cannot lose. First, **make yourself impossible to defeat: store half a year's grain, and never stake your house or your body.** Second, hold a reckoning once a year: your strengths and weaknesses, where the tide is moving, when you can fight and when you cannot, all written down. Third, engage with the orthodox and win with the unorthodox: the orthodox is your livelihood, the unorthodox is small trials that do no harm if they fail. As for joining dots into a line, that is talk after victory, not a method.
posts.vernacular: 把大家的话合起来说：计划不是画出一条非走不可的路，而是先站上一块不会输的地。第一，**先让自己不会被打垮：存够半年的生活费，别拿房子和身体去下注。**第二，每年做一次全面推演：自己的长处短处、形势往哪走、什么仗能打什么仗不能打，都写在本子上。第三，正面稳住、奇兵取胜：『正』是你的饭碗，『奇』是小规模的尝试，失败了也伤不着你。至于把点连成线，那是打赢之后说的话，当不了方法。

glossary.以正合，以奇胜: engage with the orthodox, win with the unorthodox（以正合，以奇胜）：用常规力量正面稳住阵脚，再靠出其不意的奇兵取胜。

glossary_en.engage with the orthodox and win with th: Sunzi's principle: hold the line with conventional forces, then win with surprise moves.

posts.text: 我被加扎尼加的照片说动了一半：**可选权留给事业和钱，承诺留给人和手艺。**副业可以随时换，老婆和朋友不行。剩下的照做：一，列出会让你爆仓的三样——高杠杆负债、毁掉的健康、毁掉的名声，一样都别碰。二，每月花一点小钱、小时间撒种子：见一个圈外人、试一门课、做个小项目。三，别听幸存者的路线，去问问失败的人当年漏算了什么。
posts.text_en: Gazzaniga's photos half-convinced me: **keep optionality for your career and money, and commitment for people and crafts.** You can swap side projects any time; you can't swap a wife or a friend. The rest, just do: one, list the three things that would blow you up, heavy leverage, wrecked health, a wrecked reputation, and touch none of them. Two, every month spend a little money and time sowing seeds: meet someone outside your circle, try a class, run a small project. Three, ignore the survivors' roadmaps; go ask people who failed what they missed.

posts.text: 解释器关不掉，那就让它替你干活。**大决定之前，把你的预测和理由写下来，一年后再拿出来对。**你会发现自己记忆里的『当初就知道』，大半是解释器后来补的；对上几次，你就知道该多信计划还是多信试探。另外，像塔勒布说的那样分开：可逆的事多试，不可逆的事选定了就别总回头比——比较本身会偷走满意。故事照讲，只是记得在页边写上：这是故事。
posts.text_en: You can't switch the interpreter off, so put it to work. **Before a big decision, write down your prediction and your reasons, then take it out and check a year later.** You'll find that much of what you remember as 'I knew it all along' was filled in later by the interpreter; after a few rounds you'll know whether to trust plans or experiments more. And split things as Taleb says: try lots with reversible choices, and once you've made an irreversible one, stop looking back to compare, because comparing steals satisfaction. Keep telling stories; just remember to write in the margin: this is a story.

posts.text: 我写过一篇讲话，题目是『心灵的纯洁就是只愿意一件事』。这不是要你画路线，而是要你选定一个你愿意为之负责的方向，然后承担它。孙子说先看地形，好；可别看一辈子。具体说：**给自己的犹豫定个期限，到期就选，选完给它一段不回头的时间**，比如一年。错了就再选，人是在一次次承担中成为自己的，不是在等确定性中。
posts.text_en: I wrote a discourse called Purity of Heart Is to Will One Thing. It doesn't ask you to draw a route; it asks you to choose a direction you're willing to answer for, and then to bear it. Sunzi says survey the ground first. Fine, but don't survey it for a lifetime. Concretely: **give your hesitation a deadline, choose when it runs out, and then give the choice a stretch of time with no looking back**, say a year. If it was wrong, choose again. A person becomes themselves through one act of taking responsibility after another, not by waiting for certainty.

posts.text: 听下来，大家其实在说同一件事：计划像摆碗筷，摆好了，就吃饭。吃饭的时候别还想着碗筷摆得对不对。所以，做计划的时候就好好做；做完了，把它放下。每天挑一件小事——洗碗、走路、写一封信——只做那一件。**计划落空的那天，别当成失败，那正是重新开始的初心。**你现在的位置有几成是计划来的，不重要；重要的是你此刻在不在这里。
posts.text_en: Listening to everyone, I think we're all saying the same thing: a plan is like setting the table. Once it's set, you eat. While you eat, don't keep wondering whether the table was set right. So when you make a plan, make it wholeheartedly; when it's made, put it down. Each day, pick one small thing, washing the dishes, walking, writing a letter, and do only that. **The day your plan falls through, don't call it failure; that is beginner's mind starting again.** How much of where you are was planned doesn't matter. What matters is whether you are here, now.

glossary.初心: beginner's mind（初心）：像初学者那样不预设、不自满，对一切保持开放。

glossary_en.beginner's mind: Meeting everything as a beginner does, without assumptions or self-satisfaction.

summaries.summary: **计划该管的是『不输』和『方向』，而不是路线**——七个人最后都站到了这一处。孙子的不可胜、塔勒布的不爆仓、柯维的指南针，说的都是先守住底线、认清自己要往哪去，再让路怎么走交给形势。乔布斯也承认，他敢追随好奇，前提是下行有底。分歧落在承诺上：塔勒布要处处留退路，克尔凯郭尔和加扎尼加则认为，退路本身会让人爱不起已选的那条路，有些事必须定死。铃木把问题转了个向：计划或随缘都无妨，怕的是把此刻当过道。
summaries.summary_en: **A plan should govern 'not losing' and 'direction', not the route**: that is where all seven ended up. Sunzi's invincibility, Taleb's never going bust and Covey's compass all mean the same thing: protect the floor and know where you are heading, then let circumstances decide the path. Even Jobs conceded that he could follow his curiosity because his downside had a floor. The disagreement is over commitment. Taleb wants an exit everywhere; Kierkegaard and Gazzaniga argue that exits themselves stop you from loving the road you took, and some things have to be locked in. Suzuki turned the question aside: planning or drifting is fine either way, as long as the present isn't treated as a corridor.
summaries.insight: 『你现在的位置有几成是计划来的』这道自检题，其实很难答准——加扎尼加的解释器会两头作弊：成功的部分记成『早有打算』，失败的部分记成『运气不好』。所以多数人高估了计划，也误判了偶然。更值得问的，是那些偶然**为什么偏偏落到你头上**：多半是你先去了那个地方、见了那个人、学了那门看似没用的课。好运很少砸向待在原地的人。换句话说，『走着瞧』并不被动，它要求你不停地走；规划真正能做的，是决定你往哪片地方去碰运气。
summaries.insight_en: The test question, how much of where you are was planned, is hard to answer honestly, because Gazzaniga's interpreter cheats both ways: the parts that worked get remembered as 'I always meant to', and the parts that failed as 'bad luck'. So most people overrate their plans and misread chance. The better question is **why the chance landed on you in particular**: usually because you had gone somewhere first, met someone, or taken a class that seemed useless. Luck rarely strikes people who stay put. In other words, 'finding out as you go' isn't passive; it requires you to keep going. What planning can really do is decide which patch of ground you go looking for luck in.
summaries.advice: 第一，今晚写一页纸，分两栏：左边是『绝不能输的』（如半年生活费、健康、名声、最重要的几段关系），右边是『想去试的』，写下这个月就能做的一件小事。第二，像加扎尼加说的，下次做重大决定前把预测和理由写进手机备忘录，定一个一年后的提醒，看看自己当初猜对了多少。第三，把选项分成可逆和不可逆：工作、副业、城市多试多换；伴侣、朋友、一门手艺，**选定后给它一年不回头的时间**，别边过边比。
summaries.advice_en: First, tonight, write one page in two columns. On the left, what you must never lose (say six months of living costs, your health, your reputation, your few most important relationships); on the right, what you'd like to try, with one small thing you can do this month. Second, as Gazzaniga suggests, before your next big decision put your prediction and reasons in a phone note, set a reminder for a year out, and see how much you got right. Third, sort your options into reversible and irreversible: try and switch freely with jobs, side projects and cities; with a partner, friends or a craft, **once you've chosen, give it a year without looking back**, instead of comparing as you go.

summaries.summary: 人生规划与走着瞧并非二选一：先守住健康、现金流、关系和名誉等底线，再用低成本试验探索；同时保留价值方向，并在行动时专注当下。**最可取的不是预测出正确人生，而是建立一个既不会轻易出局、又能不断修正的系统。**分歧主要在承诺应放在哪里：有人强调直觉、故事与全情投入，有人警惕幸存者偏差和事后合理化；有人主张多留选项，有人认为选择和长期承诺才能塑造自我。真正的焦点因此不是要不要计划，而是哪些事该固定、哪些事该试探，以及何时停止比较、开始承担。
summaries.insight: 比计划长短更影响结果的，其实是反馈回路的质量。很多人所谓规划，只写目标，不写假设、指标和复盘日期；所谓走着瞧，也只是被动等待，没有主动收集信号。两者看似相反，实质都无法学习。**决定人生适应力的，不是你第一次选得多准，而是你多快发现选错、又能以多小代价改正。**普通人不必辞职、搬家才算探索，可以先用周末项目、短课、访谈或兼职验证兴趣、能力与市场需求；也不必因一次试验失败就否定方向，只需更新自己对路径的判断。
summaries.advice: 一，今晚写一页『三层计划』：三年方向只写想成为什么样的人，九十天只定一个重点，本周安排一个可完成动作。二，把眼前决定分为可逆与难逆；可逆决定设两周、十小时和一笔亏得起的钱去试，难逆决定先列红线，并找一位失败过的人了解代价。三，周五留三十分钟复盘：原先假设是什么，出现了什么证据，下周是继续、调整还是停止。**先把底线和复盘日期写进日历，再允许自己大胆行动。**
summaries.summary_en: Planning and improvisation are not true opposites. A workable life strategy protects a floor—health, cash flow, close relationships, and reputation—while leaving room for inexpensive experiments. It also keeps a broad sense of direction without turning every day into a mere stepping-stone toward the future. **The goal is not to predict the right life in advance, but to build a system that keeps you from being knocked out and lets you revise course repeatedly.** The real disagreement concerns where commitment belongs. Intuition, motivating stories, and wholehearted effort can generate meaningful action, but they can also conceal survivorship bias and retrospective storytelling. Keeping options open is valuable in uncertain domains, yet identity, intimacy, and mastery often require closing alternatives and staying. The practical question is therefore not whether to plan, but what should remain fixed, what should be tested, and when continued comparison must give way to responsibility.
summaries.insight_en: The most important variable may be neither the length nor the sophistication of a plan, but the quality of its feedback loop. Many plans contain goals without assumptions, observable indicators, or review dates. Likewise, many people who claim to be taking life as it comes are not experimenting; they are simply waiting. Both approaches prevent learning. **Adaptability depends less on choosing correctly the first time than on noticing errors quickly and correcting them at a cost you can afford.** This matters especially for ordinary people who cannot casually quit a job, move across the country, or risk their savings. Exploration can happen through a weekend project, a short course, several conversations with practitioners, or limited freelance work. Such probes produce evidence about interest, ability, working conditions, and demand. If one experiment fails, it need not invalidate the larger direction; it may only show that a particular route, environment, or timing was wrong.
summaries.advice_en: First, make a one-page, three-level plan tonight. For the three-year horizon, describe only the kind of person and life you want to build. For the next ninety days, choose one priority. For this week, schedule one concrete action. Second, classify the decision in front of you as reversible or hard to reverse. If it is reversible, run a two-week test with no more than ten hours and an amount of money you can comfortably lose. If it is hard to reverse, list your non-negotiable boundaries and speak with someone whose similar choice went badly, not only someone who succeeded. Third, reserve thirty minutes on Friday to compare your original assumptions with the evidence you gathered, then explicitly choose to continue, modify, or stop. **Put your safety limits and review date on the calendar first; then give yourself permission to act boldly.**

summaries.summary: 死板的十年蓝图与蒙眼狂奔的盲目随性，在第一轮就被众人联手淘汰了。七位思想者不约而同地走向同一个落脚点：**先筑牢不败的底线，再在开阔处保持试探的弹性**——孙子的“先为不可胜”、塔勒布的九成稳妥，与乔布斯压低开销去付好奇心的学费，骨子里是同一套生存底座。真正撕开分歧的，是对待“退路”与“故事”的态度：塔勒布主张多留可选权以捕捉黑天鹅，克尔凯郭尔与加扎尼加却警告，门开得太多会让人困在比较与可能性里，失去满意与自我；乔布斯与柯维把信念故事当成行动的燃料，而科学家与风险家则冷酷地拆穿那是幸存者的事后编造。
summaries.insight: 计算机科学里的“探索与利用（Explore vs. Exploit）”算法，恰好能补上这场辩论缺失的时间轴。桌上把“留选项”和“定承诺”当成了静态的九一分账，却忽略了人生阶段与复利效应：年轻或换轨初期，剩余时间长，最优解是高比例探索（乔布斯蹭课、塔勒布撒网）；一旦试出高价值方向，就必须关门深耕（克尔凯郭尔的决断）。更关键的是，人生不是买彩票，**真正高价值的“可选权”，往往是深度承诺的副产品**。乔布斯的书法课之所以能连上线，前提是他后来对造电脑投入了偏执的承诺；没有主干的深耕，散落的点永远只是谈资。
summaries.advice: 本周就能落地的三步动作：第一，画一条“防爆仓与好奇心”分界线——核对账单，锁死半年生活费不动；同时每周划出三小时和一笔小钱，专门做一件不问回报却着迷的事。第二，拿出一张纸，**把眼下纠结的事按“可逆试错”与“不可逆承诺”分栏**：副业与新技能归左边，多试快停；伴侣与核心手艺归右边，采纳克尔凯郭尔的建议，定个期限果断关掉比较的门。第三，借用柯维与铃木的组合拳：周日晚上排好下周两块“大石头”，周一早上就把计划锁进抽屉，洗碗时只管洗碗。
summaries.summary_en: Rigid ten-year blueprints and blind, reckless drifting are both eliminated in the very first round. All seven thinkers converge on the same practical bedrock: **secure an unbeatable baseline first, then stay nimble in open territory**—Sun Tzu's "making oneself invincible," Taleb's 90% safe allocation, and Jobs's frugal funding of curiosity are ultimately the same survival architecture. Where they truly clash is over how to treat "escape hatches" and "self-narratives." Taleb champions maximum optionality to catch black swans, while Kierkegaard and Gazzaniga warn that keeping every door open traps the mind in endless comparison, costing us both satisfaction and selfhood. Likewise, Jobs and Covey harness personal stories as fuel for courage, whereas the scientist and the risk theorist coldly expose them as post-hoc illusions and survivorship bias.
summaries.insight_en: The "explore vs. exploit" trade-off in computer science supplies the missing time dimension to this debate. The panel treats optionality and commitment mainly as a static spatial split, overlooking life stages and compounding returns: when you are early in a journey with a long runway, the optimal strategy is heavy exploration (Jobs auditing classes, Taleb casting nets); once a high-value path emerges, you must close the other doors and exploit deeply (Kierkegaard's leap). More importantly, life is not a lottery ticket—**the best options are usually byproducts of deep commitment**. Jobs's calligraphy dots only connected because he later committed fanatically to building computers; without a trunk of mastery, scattered dots remain mere party trivia.
summaries.advice_en: Three concrete steps you can take this week: First, draw a clear line between your safety net and your curiosity fund—lock away six months of living expenses untouched, while carving out three hours and a tiny budget each week for something fascinating with zero KPI. Second, take a sheet of paper and **sort your current dilemmas into "reversible experiments" versus "irreversible commitments"**: treat side projects as low-cost trials, but for core relationships and craft, take Kierkegaard's cue—set a deadline to decide and shut the door on constant comparison. Third, pair Covey with Suzuki: schedule your two "big rocks" on Sunday night, then put the map away on Monday morning and give your full presence to the single task in front of you.

hooks.text: **可逆的多试，不可逆的定死**：塔勒布的可选权与加扎尼加的照片实验在哪里分界？工作、城市、伴侣、孩子、一门手艺，各该用哪种策略？
hooks.text_en: **Try the reversible, commit to the irreversible**: where is the line between Taleb's optionality and Gazzaniga's photo experiment? Jobs, cities, partners, children, a craft: which strategy fits each?

answer.lead: 先问一句：**这件事做错了，能不能在一年内低成本退回来？**能退，就当实验；退不回，就慎选、选定后少回头。

head: 情境
可逆程度
该怎么做
rows: 多试，但每次给足半年到一年再判断，别三个月就跳
大胆撒种子，小成本快验证，不喜欢就停
按塔勒布：先保证输得起，宁可错过不要赌全部
选前多看，选定后停止比较，给它不回头的时间
认真庙算：钱、时间、支持系统都先算清
设个『最短投入期』（如一年），期内不换，期满再评估

answer.tail: 两条原则：**可逆的事，速度比正确重要；不可逆的事，正确比速度重要。**选定之后，比较会偷走满意——给自己一段只投入、不回头的时间。

answer_en.lead: Ask one question first: **if this goes wrong, can I back out cheaply within a year?** If yes, treat it as an experiment; if not, choose carefully and stop looking back once you have.

head: Situation
How reversible
What to do
rows: Try things, but give each six months to a year before judging; don't jump after three months
Side projects, hobby classes, small ventures
Sow seeds boldly, test cheaply and quickly, stop if you don't like it
Hard to undo, can wipe you out
Follow Taleb: make sure you can afford to lose; better to miss out than bet everything
Look hard before choosing; once chosen, stop comparing and give it time without looking back
Do a serious reckoning: money, time and support all worked out first
Set a minimum commitment (say a year), don't switch within it, review when it ends

answer_en.tail: Two principles: **with reversible choices, speed matters more than being right; with irreversible ones, being right matters more than speed.** Once you've chosen, comparing steals satisfaction, so give yourself a stretch of commitment with no looking back.

hooks.text: **失败者没有毕业典礼**：我们的人生策略几乎全来自成功者的回忆录和演讲。如果能听到那九百九十九个人的故事，人生建议会变成什么样？
hooks.text_en: **Failures don't give commencement speeches**: nearly all our life strategy comes from winners' memoirs and speeches. If we could hear the other nine hundred and ninety-nine, what would life advice look like?

hooks.text: **反馈回路比计划长短更要紧**：只写目标不写假设和复盘日期的计划，与被动等待的『走着瞧』一样学不到东西。普通人怎样给人生装上便宜的复盘？
hooks.text_en: **The feedback loop matters more than the plan's length**: a plan with goals but no assumptions or review dates learns as little as passive drifting. How can ordinary people build cheap reviews into their lives?

hooks.text: **探索与利用的时间轴**：年轻时多探索、找到方向后关门深耕；最好的可选权往往是深度承诺的副产品。什么信号说明该从探索转向深耕了？
hooks.text_en: **Explore, then exploit**: explore heavily when young, close doors and dig in once a direction emerges; the best options are often byproducts of deep commitment. What signals that it's time to switch from exploring to digging in?

hooks.text: **计划落空之后**：裁员、生病、离婚，人失去的不只是一条路，还有计划里那个想象中的自己。该怎么告别一个没能成为的自己？
hooks.text_en: **When the plan collapses**: after a layoff, an illness or a divorce, you lose not just a path but the imagined self the plan contained. How do you say goodbye to someone you never got to become?
